newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on light volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on light volumes.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Wednesday, after another day of narrow ranges and light volumes, despite fears of renewed central bank activity.

"It looks like gold's still stuck in a range, though the bias is probably slightly negative, with some Australian producers doing some hedging in the longer dates out around ten years in the past week," Mitsui USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.
COMEX June gold ended down 10 cents at $343.30 an ounce, after trading a $343.50-342.30 range.
Estimated total COMEX gold volume was 15,000 lots.
Open interest in COMEX gold slipped 419 lots to 162,911 contracts Tuesday, after recovering a little from the lowest levels in a year at 147,494 contracts on April.
Commodity funds remain net short, analyts said, but with much smaller positions than in late 1996 and early 1997.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $341.10/60 early, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $341.00 and little changed from the New York close Tuesday.
Spot gold found support last week just below $340 an ounce, a level from which it bounced in early January also.
But gold has failed to climb back above the $350 level, with renewed concerns emerging about European central bank activity this week.
However, the Dutch central bank Tuesday denied it had been selling its gold reserves again, after confirming a sale of around 300 tonnes back in January.

Overnight, the Bundesbank also reiterated its opposition to IMF gold sales, arguing, in its 1996 annual report just published, against the planned use of IMF gold to help fund a third world debt relief program.
But UBS's London analyst, Andy Smith, issued a report saying gold total demonitization was well under way, like silver's 100 years ago.

Gold equities continued to lose ground Wednesday also, with the Philadelphia Stock Exchange's gold and silver index of North American mining stocks (.XAU) sliding to a low of 94.10 near the close, its lowest level since September 1993.
COMEX May silver ended up 1.0 cent at $4.725, after seeing a $4.675-4.740 range, with support in the contract still seen around $4.670 and resistance around $4.80.
Most activity in silver was focused on the May/July roll, traders said. First notice day for May silver is April 30.
NYMEX July platinum ended down $2.00 at $374.40, on further light profit taking, while NYMEX June palladium gained 25 cents to $155.00, but the physical market remained very tight, traders said.
Platinum and palladium short term lease rates remained around 10-12 percent for both metals, with the issue of Russian supplies still unresolved, refining sources said.
